title: Machine-learning eplet risk score links HLA mismatches to donor-specific antibodies
summary: Across six liver, lung and kidney transplant cohorts from two centers (978 donor-recipient pairs), certain mismatched HLA eplets were strongly linked to donor-specific antibody development while others were weakly linked, with a consistent trend across organs. Machine learning used these hierarchical associations to build an eplet risk score that outperformed traditional eplet mismatch assessments. T cell proliferation in mixed lymphocyte reactions correlated with the score and was reduced by antibody inhibition of a mismatched DSA-associated eplet. The abstract gives no numeric performance values or validation split.
ai_technology: Machine learning built an eplet risk score from mismatched HLA eplet associations

evidence.tested: Retrospective association and machine-learning scoring in six transplant cohorts, with an in vitro mixed lymphocyte reaction correlation.
evidence.unknown: Validation split and numeric performance; prospective clinical use; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning derived the eplet risk score from eplet-level associations.
